Rob You Deaf

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
How one little boy lost his hearing in a highway robbery

Unique Selling Point:
Interview with family who were ambushed on the N4 in February. This ongoing problem plagues weekend travellers between Mpumalanga and Pretoria. Gangs of robbers place dangerous rocks and spikes on the N4 near Bronkhorstspruit so that cars will be forced to pull over. Once travellers have stopped to inspect the damage they rob them at gunpoint. But this time, they took a little boy's hearing.

Summary:
Evan van Heerden was born on 3 May 2016. 11 months later he was diagnosed with bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss. He was born deaf. He was assessed and accepted by the Ear Institute Cochlear Implant Unit. After several fund raising events, including two live shows (Bok van Blerk performed), two golf days and private donations by friends and family members, Evan was able to receive first the right ear implant in 2017, and in 2019 the left ear implant. His mother Marlize upgraded her Discovery Medical Aid plan, and was able to receive an upgrade for his hearing aid in February 2021. Discovery paid out over R200 000 for his hearing aid (he is eligible for an upgrade every 3 years)

Further information:
On 28 February 4 year-old Evan van Heerden was asleep in the back seat as his parents drove back to Pretoria from a weekend in Sabie. At about 10.00pm their car tyre blew. They pulled over and found no spare tyre or jack in the boot. They called their friends in Centurion for help, and Tod they they were 16km away from the Diamond Hill toll plaza. Feeling unsafe they drove on a few hundred meters at a time, before they decided they would damage the wheel rim. At 10.45pm they were attacked by 7 gun-wielding men who forced them out of the car and made them sit on the verge while they ransacked the car.
They stole a solar battery, solar inverter, all their cellphones, wallets and Evan's mother's handbag containing his 2 hearing aids and 6 batteries. (she had taken out his hearing aids as he was asleep)
SAPS was patrolling the highway and came to their assistance. They confirmed that it was definitely spikes that damaged their wheel, and found 7 long nails inside the wheel. They say this has been a problem on that stretch of the N$ for the last 3 years.
This robbery has left Evan without his hearing aids. Although he still has access to one old hearing aid, his speech and development has suffered another setback. Evan will only be able to upgrade to a new left hearing aid in April 2022 and a new right ear hearing aid in February 2024

Script:


ROB YOU DEAF

V/O: When Evan van Heerden was born in May 2016 he was a healthy little boy, and Marlize Joubert’s first baby.

Marlize: As time went on and he got older, we saw delays in his development.

V/O: By the age of 11 months he still wasn’t sitting.

Marlize: We actually ended up at a neurologist. She was the one who sent us to Steve Biko for his first hearing test. And we found out that he actually has a hearing loss.

V/O: In 2017 Evan was referred to the Ear Institute in Pretoria for evaluation. They diagnosed bilateral sensori-neural hearing loss.

Catherine: His hearing loss originates in the inner ear, specifically the cochlear.

V/O: Dr Catherine van Dijk is the Head of the Cochlear Implant Division.

Catherine: So a cochlear implant would be the solution for him because it bypasses the damaged part, the inner ear, and then the sound can go directly to the brain for him to interpret.

Link: Evan was born deaf. In the past this would have condemned him to a life of silence, but now cochlear implants are an everyday miracle. But that miracle doesn’t come cheap.

Catherine: So the cost of a cochlear implant is around about R380 000. That includes the device, the surgery and the hospitalization.

V/O: Evan’s medical aid paid just over R300 000 of the cost, and the rest was covered by a donation from the Foundation for Children with Hearing Loss and funds raised through two charity concerts and two golf days. His cochlear implant was switched on in December 2017.

Marlize: It was really amazing. He just looked up and then went on with whatever he’s busy with.

Sfx: Music

Marlize With the hearing aid the words started coming. He started sitting and walking by himself.

V/O: With the help of a speech therapist Evan progressed even further. In 2019 he got his second cochlear implant in his right ear, and last month received an upgrade to the processor for his left ear. Their new medical aid covered all costs.

Catherine: These days the biggest design changes are made to the outside part, the processors, and this is important, this is why we wanted Evan to upgrade so that he could have the latest technology.

V/O; Two weeks after his upgrade the family went away for the weekend. A cousin joined them in Sabie in Mpumalanga, and on Sunday the 28th of February they drove home to Pretoria.

Link: During the day this stretch of the N4 near the Diamond Hill toll Plaza looks quite boring and unremarkable. But at night, anything is possible.
V/O: Marlize was driving, while the others were asleep. They had just passed Bronkhorstspruit at about 10:00pm when a tyre burst and she was forced to pull over.

Marlize: We unpacked everything in the boot to get to the spare wheel and realised that there’s no jack and no spanner.

V/O: Feeling unsafe, they called friends in Centurion to come to their rescue while Evan’s father Schalk checked his GPS.

Marlize: We saw that we were 16km away from the Diamond Hill tollgate but we at least just wanted to move forward instead of sitting at one place. He moved it forward and then got out to check the tire.

V/O: Realizing they were damaging the wheel rim they decided to stop and wait.

Marlize: I was on the phone, his cousin and Evan were both sleeping in the back seat, and all of a sudden Schalk’s door gets pulled open. He gets forced out of the car with a gun. And all of a sudden obviously I check to my side to see if anybody’s there, and they also pull my door open.

V/O: They were made to sit in the grass at gunpoint while the rest of the gang ransacked their car.

Marlize: And the guy actually asked us, he was like ‘what are you guys doing out on the highway this time of the night? You guys know it’s dangerous.’ He was actually the one that was pointing his firearm straight at me with Evan in my arms.

Claire: Were you worried that he might shoot you?

Marlize: Well in that situation, it’s going to sound harsh, you prepare yourself for all of you to die that night including your child. You don’t see any other way out, you know. At that moment that’s how it’s going to happen, because that’s how it always happens.

Claire: During this incident were other cars driving past?

Marlize: There were a lot of cars driving past. But what can you do in that situation? Because if I’ve got my family in the car and I see that…you protect your own family, that’s the way we live now.

V/O: Within minutes the gang disappeared into the long grass, carrying all the family’s possessions, including both of Evan’s sound processors.

Marlize: I take them off when he sleeps.

Claire: So you had taken them off and put them where?

Marlize: In my handbag.

V/O: It was only when they reached the Bronkhorstspruit Police Station that they realised their tyre hadn’t burst, but had been ripped apart by spikes deliberately placed in the road by their attackers.

Link: This ambush was not an isolated incident and Police have warned motorists to look out for spikes placed on the N4 highway. The trouble is - you can’t always see them - especially at night.

TMPD: N4 Diamond Hill, N4 Diamond Hill, be safe friends and family. This is what they do. This is what we’ve got ne N4…ama-spikes, and then all covered in plastic…only to find they are spikes. Immediately when you stop, they hijack, they take your belongings and everything.

Brigadier: We are aware of this and we’re working very hard together with the Tshwane Metro Police Department patrolling the area. And that is why we’ve noticed a decline in the number of incidents lately.

V/O: According to Brigadier Mathapelo Peters Bronkhorstspruit police have recorded 14 incidents in recent months,

Brigadier: However we have had cases reported in different police stations as well, so this could be more, but it’s not more than 20.

Claire: So what advice would you give motorists now that we’re going into Easter?

Brigadier: We’ll be focusing on those hotspots and crime areas where we know that a specific pattern of crime has been picked up. But what I want to stress for now we are still under Level 1 of the Lockdown. There is still a curfew. So other than just that safety in terms of avoiding being robbed and all that, people should also respect the lockdown regulations and rather stay at home.

V/O: But for Evan it’s too late.

Marlize: He actually asked me two days after this incident for his ears, for - we call it his ears - for the hearing aids. And I couldn’t give it to him because I didn’t have it.

V/O: Currently Evan is left with only the old processor for his right ear.

Link: Having met Evan it’s quite clear that the loss of both his “ears” has been a setback. Replacing them is costly, but the longer he waits the further he will regress.

Catherine: I think his parents can already pick up a change in his behaviour. He will be more frustrated because he cannot communicate his needs, he is not always aware of what they are saying to him, what they want from him. I would think in three month’s-time you would already hear a change in his intelligibility of his speech. And round about six months, he's going to be a different child.
